content.text:
What kind of story is Alice in Wonderland?

Alice in Wonderland is a fantasy adventure in which a girl named Alice tumbles down a rabbit hole and meets extraordinary beings like a talking rabbit, a hatter, and a queen. It is a classic that gives free rein to imagination and curiosity.

content.alt: Alice in Wonderland - The original story of Alice in Wonderland
content.text:
The original story of Alice in Wonderland

The original is Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, published by the British author Lewis Carroll in 1865. With its distinctive characters—the White Rabbit with his pocket watch, the tea-drinking Hatter, and the Queen of Hearts crying "Off with their heads!"—it has been loved around the world.

content.alt: Alice in Wonderland - Alice in Wonderland story summary
content.text:
Alice in Wonderland story summary

Following the rabbit with the pocket watch into a hole, Alice experiences one wondrous thing after another—growing bigger and smaller, joining a strange tea party, and getting caught up in the Queen of Hearts' trial. In the end she discovers it was all a dream, waking up to finish her delightful adventure.

content.alt: Alice in Wonderland - The lesson of Alice in Wonderland
content.text:
The lesson of Alice in Wonderland

The core message is the joy of exploring new things with curiosity, and holding on to your own thinking even amid the nonsense. Imagine together "What if impossible things happened?" and grow creativity side by side.

content.alt: Alice in Wonderland - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Acting out each character with an exaggerated voice brings the whimsical mood to life. Let your child imagine "How would it feel to grow bigger and smaller?" and laugh together at the nonsensical scenes to share the joy of imagination. Best suited for ages 5 to 7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Alice in Wonderland good for?
A. Best suited for ages 5 to 7. Its whimsical developments and rich imagination are great for growing creativity.

Q. Won't the story be too complicated?
A. Picture books for young children pare it down to the key scenes so the focus stays on the joy of imagination.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Drawing your own imagined Wonderland, mimicking the characters' voices, and "grow big, shrink small" body play all work great.

Classic tales to read together

If you enjoyed this story, try reading these classic tales together too.

  • The Frog Prince
  • The Ant and the Grasshopper
  • The Selfish Giant
  • Gulliver's Travels
